## Context and classification

The later Uncovering Cicada Wiki page [Mentioned PRIMES](https://uncovering-cicada.fandom.com/wiki/Mentioned_PRIMES) labels this paste as **MISSING PRIMES** and separately links the raw **PRIMES TELNET OUTPUT** paste with ID xGY4pbHV. The later [Telnet Prompt](https://uncovering-cicada.fandom.com/wiki/The_Telnet_Prompt) page also links xGY4pbHV as the output of the primes command. These wiki pages are secondary indexes, not original service captures.

This is a separate, platform-timestamped **2013 participant artifact**. It establishes that the exact 180-prime omission list was circulating by 14 January 2013. It does **not** contain the raw Telnet response, command prompt, host, port, response framing, server source, or a creator signature. The date is Pastebin's displayed creation metadata, not a cryptographic timestamp; the author is anonymous.

The list is mathematically the consecutive prime interval p21 through p200 (73 through 1223). This independently supports the *existence and contemporary discussion* of the missing-prime set, but not the exact behavior of the first-onion service, the intentionality of the omission, or any LP2 key/operation.

## Exact missing artifact

The raw **PRIMES TELNET OUTPUT** paste with ID xGY4pbHV is the specific next artifact to recover. The later wiki links to it, but the normal page and raw endpoints were not retrievable in this investigation, and exact-ID web searches did not surface an archived copy. A byte-preserved 2013 Telnet session/packet capture or original first-onion server source would also resolve the command grammar and output framing.

Do not substitute the 26 January 2013 participant TCP-server challenge: its signed BASE29, DH, and NEXT protocol is a different service, not authentication for the first-onion NUMBER/PRIMES commands.
